root_causes: The question's proper noun 'Sui Vanguard' has no lexical or entity anchor anywhere in the memory DB; the perception/captioning pipeline described this boss only generically ('boss (molten giant)'), never reading or transcribing its in-game name banner.

The DB contains an unrelated but strongly matching entity, 'Tiger Vanguard (虎先锋)', with its own visually similar post-boss body-cultivation-allocation scene; 3 of 5 rollouts converged on it purely because it is the only entity literally containing 'vanguard'.

Two rollouts' semantic_search did surface a hit close to the true clue window (episodes:30sec:002482, 74460s) but neither rollout drilled into that lead before committing to a different, wrong scene.

No rollout ran a systematic sweep of ALL body-cultivation-allocation scenes in the video to cross-check which one immediately follows a distinctive boss/location context matching 'Sui'; each rollout stopped at the first plausible scene its search chain produced.
what_worked: All rollouts correctly followed the general-retrieval / locating-time-intervals / semantic-search / visual-verification skill workflow and used clip_qa to visually read the stat name from the on-screen node description before submitting, rather than guessing blind.

transferable_lessons: When a question boss/entity name yields zero or only a loosely related entity-table match, treat that as a red flag that the DB's proper-noun coverage may be incomplete rather than assuming the best lexical match (e.g. 'Tiger Vanguard') is the intended entity.

When multiple visually similar candidate scenes exist for a templated in-game action (e.g. 'post-boss stat allocation'), enumerate ALL of them across the full timeline (via run_sql over event_chains/entities matching 'boss defeat' broadly) before committing, rather than stopping at the first clip_qa that returns a plausible-sounding answer.

Do not discard a semantic_search hit just because subsequent broader queries return more results elsewhere; when a specific-term query (e.g. containing the exact rare proper noun from the question) returns a hit, that hit deserves priority follow-up over generic-term hits.

For short temporal_certificate windows (~10s), a single clip_qa call spanning that exact window may catch the player still browsing/hovering multiple stat options rather than the moment of confirmation; widen the clip_qa window slightly around the clue interval and instruct clip_qa to identify the specific node with a confirmed/committed state (e.g. resource-point counter decreasing, 已参悟 status appearing) rather than just the currently-hovered tooltip.
